title: One-Week Low-Sodium Meal Plan
summary: This week's plan focuses on reducing sodium by using herbs, spices, and lemon for flavor instead of salt. It supports weight management with portion-controlled meals rich in vegetables, lean protein, and whole grains, with dinners making leftovers for the next day's lunch.

recipes.title: Quinoa Salad with Chickpeas and Avocado
ingredients: 100 g chickpeas, no salt added, rinsed
steps: Place 150 g water into mixing bowl. Insert simmering basket, weigh in 75 g quinoa and rinse under tap water. Cook 15 min/100°C/speed 4.
Use spatula to remove simmering basket and set quinoa aside to cool slightly.
In a bowl, combine the cooked quinoa, 100 g chickpeas, 100 g cherry tomatoes, and 50 g baby spinach.
Slice half an avocado. Dress the salad with 15 ml lemon juice, 15 ml olive oil, and a pinch of black pepper. Mix gently and serve.
recipes.why: This salad is based on whole grains, plant-based protein, and fresh vegetables, with no added salt.
recipes.evidence: Carbohydrates in the diet should come primarily from whole grains, vegetables, fruits and pulses (like beans, lentils, and peas). [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Steamed Salmon with Broccoli and Brown Rice
steps: Place 800 g water into the mixing bowl. Insert simmering basket and weigh in 150 g brown rice. Cook 20 min/100°C/speed 4.
Meanwhile, place 250 g salmon fillets on Varoma tray lined with wet baking paper. Season with black pepper, 2 g mixed herbs, and top with lemon slices.
Place 300 g broccoli florets into the Varoma dish. At the end of the rice cooking time, assemble the Varoma and cook 15 min/Varoma/speed 1.

Remove the Varoma and simmering basket. Serve one portion consisting of half the salmon (125 g), half the broccoli (150 g), and half the cooked rice, drizzled with 7.5 ml olive oil. Store the remaining portion in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
recipes.why: This meal includes fish for healthy fats and a large portion of vegetables, with no added salt.
recipes.evidence: Everyone older than 10 years of age should aim for at least 400 grams of fruits and vegetables per day. [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Leftover Steamed Salmon with Broccoli and Brown Rice
steps: Enjoy the leftover portion of salmon, broccoli, and rice cold. Alternatively, to reheat, place the food in the Varoma dish, add 500 g water to the mixing bowl, and steam for 8-10 min/Varoma/speed 1.
recipes.why: This meal includes fish for healthy fats and a large portion of vegetables, with no added salt.
recipes.evidence: Everyone older than 10 years of age should aim for at least 400 grams of fruits and vegetables per day. [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Chicken and Vegetable Sauté
steps: Place 1 garlic clove and 75 g onion into mixing bowl, chop 3 sec/speed 5. Scrape down sides.
Add 20 g olive oil and sauté 3 min/120°C/speed 1.
Add 250 g chicken breast and cook without measuring cup 5 min/120°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Add 150 g bell pepper, 150 g zucchini, 20 ml apple cider vinegar, and a pinch of black pepper. Cook 8 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Serve half of the chicken and vegetable sauté immediately. Store the remaining portion in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
recipes.why: This dish combines lean protein with a variety of vegetables, using vinegar and pepper for flavor instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: A healthy dietary pattern includes a wide variety of vegetables and fruits. [American Heart Association — Diet and lifestyle recommendations]

recipes.title: Leftover Chicken and Vegetable Sauté
steps: Enjoy the leftover sauté cold. To reheat, place the portion in the mixing bowl and heat for 4-5 min/90°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
recipes.why: This dish combines lean protein with a variety of vegetables, using vinegar and pepper for flavor instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: A healthy dietary pattern includes a wide variety of vegetables and fruits. [American Heart Association — Diet and lifestyle recommendations]

recipes.title: Hearty Lentil Soup
steps: Place 150 g onion, 120 g carrots, and 1 garlic clove into mixing bowl. Chop 5 sec/speed 5.
Scrape down sides, add 15 g olive oil and sauté 3 min/120°C/speed 1.
Add 150 g rinsed lentils, 700 g low-sodium vegetable stock, 2 g mixed herbs, and a pinch of black pepper.
Cook 30 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Serve half of the soup immediately. Allow the remaining half to cool before storing in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
recipes.why: This soup is based on pulses (like beans, lentils, and peas) and vegetables, and uses low-sodium stock and herbs for flavor.
recipes.evidence: In many high-income countries, and increasingly in low- and middle-income countries, a significant proportion of sodium in the diet comes from processed foods. [WHO — Sodium reduction (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Leftover Hearty Lentil Soup
steps: Pour the leftover soup into the mixing bowl and reheat for 5-6 min/90°C/speed 1 before serving.
recipes.why: This soup is based on pulses (like beans, lentils, and peas) and vegetables, and uses low-sodium stock and herbs for flavor.
recipes.evidence: In many high-income countries, and increasingly in low- and middle-income countries, a significant proportion of sodium in the diet comes from processed foods. [WHO — Sodium reduction (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Turkey Slices with Sautéed Zucchini and Pepper
ingredients: 200 g turkey breast slices, low sodium
steps: Place 1 garlic clove into mixing bowl and chop 3 sec/speed 7.
Scrape down sides, add 15 g olive oil and sauté 2 min/120°C/speed 1.
Add 200 g zucchini, 150 g bell pepper, 2 g mixed herbs, and a pinch of black pepper. Cook 10 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Add 200 g low-sodium turkey slices, tearing them into pieces, and cook for a further 2 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Serve half of the turkey and vegetables immediately. Store the remaining portion in an airtight container in the refrigerator.
recipes.why: A light meal with lean protein and vegetables, seasoned with herbs instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: A healthy dietary pattern includes foods prepared with little or no salt. [American Heart Association — Diet and lifestyle recommendations]

recipes.title: Leftover Turkey Slices with Sautéed Zucchini and Pepper
steps: Enjoy the leftover meal cold. Alternatively, to reheat, place the portion in the mixing bowl and heat for 4-5 min/90°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
recipes.why: A light meal with lean protein and vegetables, seasoned with herbs instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: A healthy dietary pattern includes foods prepared with little or no salt. [American Heart Association — Diet and lifestyle recommendations]

recipes.title: Whole-Wheat Pasta with Tomato and Bean Sauce
ingredients: 200 g cannellini beans, no salt added, rinsed
steps: Add 1200 g water to mixing bowl. Heat 10 min/100°C/speed 1. Add 150 g pasta through hole in lid and cook for time indicated on packet/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon. Drain and set aside.
Clean and dry mixing bowl. Place 1 garlic clove and 75 g onion into bowl, chop 3 sec/speed 5. Scrape down sides.
Add 15 g olive oil and sauté 3 min/120°C/speed 1.
Add 250 g cherry tomatoes and 2 g mixed herbs. Cook 10 min/100°C/speed 1.
Add 200 g cannellini beans and blend 10 sec/speed 4 for a slightly chunky sauce. Heat 1 min/90°C/speed 2.
Serve half of the cooked pasta with half of the sauce. Store the remaining pasta and sauce separately in airtight containers in the refrigerator.
recipes.why: This dish uses whole-wheat pasta for fiber and adds plant-based protein from beans, with no added salt.
recipes.evidence: Follow an overall healthy dietary pattern that includes whole grains and products made up mostly of whole grains rather than refined grains. [American Heart Association — Diet and lifestyle recommendations]

recipes.title: Leftover Whole-Wheat Pasta with Tomato and Bean Sauce
steps: Place the leftover sauce in the mixing bowl and heat for 4 min/90°C/speed 2. Serve over the leftover pasta, which can be eaten cold or reheated separately (e.g., in a microwave).
recipes.why: This dish uses whole-wheat pasta for fiber and adds plant-based protein from beans, with no added salt.
recipes.evidence: Follow an overall healthy dietary pattern that includes whole grains and products made up mostly of whole grains rather than refined grains. [American Heart Association — Diet and lifestyle recommendations]

recipes.title: Steamed Cod with Cherry Tomatoes and Spinach
steps: Place 500 g water in mixing bowl. Assemble Varoma.
On the Varoma tray, place 150 g cod fillet, 100 g cherry tomatoes, and sliced garlic. Season with black pepper.
Steam 15 min/Varoma/speed 1, or until cod is cooked through.
Place 100 g baby spinach in a serving bowl. Top with the hot cod and tomatoes; the heat will wilt the spinach.
Drizzle with 10 ml olive oil and serve.
recipes.why: A simple meal featuring fish and vegetables, flavored with garlic and pepper instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: Follow an overall healthy dietary pattern that includes healthy protein sources like beans, peas, lentils, nuts, fish, and seafood. [American Heart Association — Diet and lifestyle recommendations]

recipes.title: Scrambled Eggs with Spinach and Avocado
steps: Insert butterfly whisk. Place 2 eggs, 30 ml milk, and a pinch of black pepper into mixing bowl. Mix 10 sec/speed 3.
Add 5 g butter and 50 g baby spinach. Cook 4 min/90°C/speed 1.
Check for desired consistency, cooking 1-2 min longer if needed.
Serve immediately with 1/2 sliced avocado on the side.
recipes.why: This meal provides protein from eggs and includes vegetables, with no added salt.
recipes.evidence: Protein can come from a mix of animal and plant sources. [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

recipes.title: Tofu and Vegetable Curry with Brown Rice
steps: Place 400 g water into mixing bowl. Insert simmering basket, weigh in 75 g brown rice. Cook 20 min/100°C/speed 4. Set aside and keep warm.
Clean and dry mixing bowl. Place 75 g onion and 1 garlic clove into bowl, chop 3 sec/speed 5. Scrape down sides.
Add 10 g olive oil and sauté 3 min/120°C/speed 1.
Add 60 g carrot, 100 g broccoli, and 200 g low-sodium vegetable stock. Cook 10 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Add 150 g tofu, 2 g mixed herbs, and a pinch of black pepper. Cook 3 min/100°C/Reverse/speed spoon.
Serve the curry with the cooked brown rice.
recipes.why: A plant-based meal with tofu for protein, plus whole grains and vegetables, flavored with herbs instead of salt.
recipes.evidence: For many adults, a shift towards more plant-based sources of protein may bring health benefits, particularly when the shift is away from red meat. [WHO — Healthy diet (fact sheet)]

movement: Monday: Start the week with a 20-minute brisk walk in your neighborhood.
Tuesday: Increase your walk to 25 minutes today.
Wednesday: A 20-minute brisk walk, plus 10 minutes of strength: 2 sets of 10 wall push-ups and 10 bodyweight squats.
Thursday: Aim for a continuous 30-minute brisk walk.
Friday: Another 30-minute brisk walk. Try a different route to keep it interesting.
Saturday: A 25-minute brisk walk, plus 10 minutes of strength: 2 sets of 10 lunges (each leg) and a 30-second plank.
Sunday: Enjoy a relaxing 30-minute walk at a comfortable pace.
